description:
Three independent conflicts at distinct tensions, where grounding and tension are deliberately **anti-correlated**: the highest-tension dispute is the one whose target is best corroborated, and the lowest-tension one has a thinly-held target.

Stage 4's first result rested on a single conflict, which cannot discriminate any ordering — every arm attends to the only thing available. The selection blindness established in Stage 0.5 (`stake_of` averages salience, so stake cannot see grounding) only bites where the loop has a *choice*, and only under a budget too small to reach everything.

So this is the web where the adversarial question is actually askable: **under scarce attention, does a tension-driven loop spend its budget on the disputes whose targets are best evidenced?** A driven arm should, an inverted arm should not, and random should sit between them — which makes the measurement falsifiable rather than definitional.

expect.note: Structural. What fraction of a scarce budget lands on well-grounded targets is the dependent variable and is computed.
